rv.q: This Three Penny is practically perfect, for the aficionado and the newbie.
I must admit that the show might not be everyone's cup of tea, but the sheer array of talent on the Theo Ubique stage, and Anzevino's exquisitely directed production, are nothing short of stellar.
This is especially a top pick for those of us who enjoy their musicals up-front-and-close—very, very close.

With all its conflicts and contradictions–including the fact that this anti-capitalist broadside is being presented by a non-union company–this is still the single best Brecht production I've ever seen on a Chicago stage.

While Brecht may have written with longer attention spans in mind, this production is intentional and specific with each moment, pulling the show along through compelling character work and sheer roguish charm.
I think it is going to be one of those productions either really loved or not.
To use a line from "My Fair Lady", " I doubted they could do it, BUT succeed they did!".

cn.t: Theo Ubique's production earns praise for exceptional performances and stellar direction, though some question whether Brecht and Weill's 1928 satire remains biting social commentary or feels like dated melodrama from a modern perspective.
